packages.title: A typed step is never lost
brief: Context: P21 (b8 round 1) replaced the add-step dialog with an inline `Añadir paso` field in ChecklistEditor. Enter adds a step; leaving the field (`_addFocus` listener → `_addLeft` → `_addStep(next: false)`) commits it. The reviewer found two ways a step typed without Enter is still lost. P21's implementer reported the first as a known limit. No copy changes in this package: no ARB edits, no gen-l10n.
UX-621 (R1B-1, S3), the capture sheet's result card drops a step typed without Enter:

- Where: App/lib/widgets/checklist_editor.dart `_addStep` (about :62-72), and `_CaptureResultState._save` in App/lib/screens/voice_task_screen.dart (about :2121-2134; the card's `enabled: !_saving` is at about :2503).

- What happens: the user types a step in `Añadir paso` on a result card and taps `Añadir al calendario` (key `save-drafts`) without pressing Enter. On Android, a touch outside a text field doesn't move focus, so the text is still in the field. `_save` reads `ready` from `_items` straight away, then sets `_saving` through setState. The card rebuilds disabled, so ChecklistEditor's `onChanged` is null. The field then loses focus, and `_addStep` clears the text and calls the null `onChanged`. The step is gone, and the drafts were already read anyway.
- Fix 1, in ChecklistEditor `_addStep`: when `widget.onChanged == null`, return before `_add.clear()`, so a disabled editor never throws text away. Keep the rest of `_addStep` as it is.

- Fix 2, in `_CaptureResultState._save`, do what `TaskEditor._save` already does (App/lib/widgets/task_editor.dart:255-263). Before anything reads `_items`, and before the setState that sets `_saving`, mark the save as started with a plain field and no setState (reuse `_saving` the way TaskEditor does, or add a private bool). Then call `FocusScope.of(context).unfocus()`, `await Future<void>.microtask(() {})`, and return if `!mounted`. Only then compute `ready` from `_items` and go on as today, including the existing `if (_saving || ready.isEmpty) return;` re-entry and empty checks. Two quick taps must still save once. The focus listener's `_change(draft)` updates `_items` synchronously inside its setState, so `_items` already holds the step after that microtask.

- `_saveAsWritten` (`Guardar tal cual`, about :1289) belongs to the listening and processing state (`_VoiceTaskScreenState`). It runs while the assistant is slow or has failed, when no result card or ChecklistEditor is on screen. Leave it alone, unless you find a path where it runs with a result card visible. If you do, apply the same unfocus-and-microtask step there, and say so in your notes.
UX-622 (R1B-2, S2), toggling `Más detalles` erases a half-typed step in the task form:

- Where: App/lib/widgets/task_editor.dart. One ChecklistEditor sits in the collapsed branch `if (!_detailsExpanded) ...[` and shows when `_checklist.isNotEmpty` (about :583-589). The other sits in the expanded branch `if (_detailsExpanded) ...[` (about :661-666). Neither has a key, and they sit at different places in the Column.

- What happens: tapping `Más detalles` / `Menos detalles` (key `task-more-details`) disposes one editor and builds the other. Text typed in `Añadir paso` without Enter is lost, because `dispose` removes the focus listener before it can commit.

- Fix: add one `final _steps = GlobalKey();` to the TaskEditor state, with a short comment like the one in App/lib/widgets/capture_review_editor.dart:45-47. Pass `key: _steps` to both ChecklistEditor instances. The two branches are exclusive (`!_detailsExpanded` / `_detailsExpanded`), so the key is never in the tree twice. Don't move either editor and don't change the order P21 set.

Don't touch: capture_review_editor.dart (its `_steps` key from P21 is right); the checklist's inline rename and ⋮ menu; the sheet's landing, Deshacer and messages; free_voice, capture_id and the storage lines; any ARB file.
acceptance: Widget test (review_tasks_test.dart): in the capture sheet's result card, in Spanish at 1× on 360×740, type `Passport` in `add-checklist-item` and tap `save-drafts` without pressing Enter. The saved task's checklist contains one step titled `Passport`.
Widget test: the same check with two quick taps on `save-drafts` saves the task once, with the step.
Widget test (checklist_test.dart): a ChecklistEditor with `onChanged: null` and text in `add-checklist-item` keeps that text in the field when the field loses focus.

Widget test: editing a task with one step, type `Coat` in `add-checklist-item` without Enter and tap `task-more-details`. Afterwards either the add field still reads `Coat` or the checklist holds a step `Coat`, and the text isn't lost. Tap `task-more-details` again (`Menos detalles`): the same holds, and there's no duplicate `Coat` step.
Code: both ChecklistEditor instances in task_editor.dart pass the same GlobalKey. `_CaptureResultState._save` unfocuses and awaits a microtask before it reads `_items`.
deviceChecks: On an Android phone, in the capture result card: type a step in `Añadir paso`, tap `Añadir al calendario` without Enter, open the saved task, and the step is there.

packages.title: Sign-in again says why, keeps the email, and Back changes nothing
brief: Context: P30 (b8 round 1) keeps the open screens when the server ends the session. `_showSignInAgain` (App/lib/main.dart:298-311) pushes `PopScope(canPop: false, child: LoginScreen())` over them, and `_closeSignInAgain` pops it when the same account signs back in. The reviewer found that this route is the ordinary cold-start sign-in. It doesn't say why it appeared or that the open screen comes back, and the email field is empty. Pressing Back erases the only explanation: the outer PopScope blocks the pop, so LoginScreen's own `onPopInvokedWithResult` (login_screen.dart:279-281) runs with `didPop == false` and calls `_mode()`, and `_mode()` calls `clearError()`, which removes the `requestError(session)` banner below the submit button.

- LoginScreen (login_screen.dart:18-19): add a named parameter `final bool signInAgain;`, default `false`. In main.dart `_showSignInAgain`, build `LoginScreen(signInAgain: true)` inside the same outer `PopScope(canPop: false)`. Cold-start sign-in keeps using `LoginScreen()` unchanged.

- Prefill: when `widget.signInAgain`, in `initState` set `_email.text` to the expired account's email (`ref.read(authProvider).account?.email`, Account.email in App/lib/services/api_client.dart:72). Leave it empty when there's no account.

- The reason line: when `widget.signInAgain`, the text under the heading that today shows `strings.authPitch` in sign-in and create modes (login_screen.dart, the `Text(_recover ? strings.recoveryHelp : strings.authPitch, …)` under the heading, about :335-343) shows a new key `signInAgainReason` instead. Show it in sign-in and create modes. In recovery, keep `recoveryHelp`. This replaces the sales pitch, which means nothing to someone who already uses the app, so nothing is added to the screen. Use the same position and style as `authPitch`. Drive the line from `widget.signInAgain` alone, never from `auth.error`, so typing, a failed attempt and Back can't hide it.

- Copy, new key `signInAgainReason`, as whole sentences. EN `You were signed out. Sign in again to pick up where you left off.` / ES `Tu sesión se ha cerrado. Vuelve a entrar y seguirás donde lo dejaste.` / CA `S’ha tancat la sessió. Torna a entrar i continuaràs on ho havies deixat.` (typographic apostrophe, as the catalogs write it). Add a description in app_en.arb: shown above the sign-in form when the session ended while the app was open. Then run `flutter gen-l10n`.

- Don't say it twice: on this route, don't show the outcome banner for the expiry's own error, meaning `widget.signInAgain && _error == null && auth.error != null && requestProblem(auth.error!) == 'session'`. An error from the user's own attempt (credentials, network…) lands in `_error` through `_run`, and still shows as today. Don't change the `requestError` copy: other places still use `session`.

- Back: change the inner callback to `if (!didPop && !busy && (_register || _recover)) _mode();`. Back in create or recovery still returns to sign-in, as today. Back in sign-in mode no longer calls `_mode()` / `clearError()`. On the sign-in-again route it does nothing at all, because the outer PopScope blocks it. On the cold-start root it leaves the app, as before. Leave `canPop: !_register && !_recover` as it is.

Don't touch: `_closeSignInAgain`, the `expired` handling in auth_provider.dart, the session-key rebuild for a different account (main.dart:373-383), Google sign-in, the language button, the server field, and the cold-start login's heading and pitch. Don't add a warning about signing in with a different account: see plan.md, Round 2 (b8), Noted.
Mind the layout: the reason line is about as long as `authPitch` in ES and CA. Check that it wraps cleanly at 2× text on 320 dp in Catalan; there's no auth preview for this route.
acceptance: Widget test (session_resume_test.dart): signed in as `ana@example.com`, invalidate the session while the shell is open. In Spanish, the sign-in route shows `Tu sesión se ha cerrado. Vuelve a entrar y seguirás donde lo dejaste.`, and the `account-email` field holds `ana@example.com`.

Widget test: on that route, simulate system Back. The route is still shown, the reason line is still visible, the email is still prefilled, and the open screen underneath (for example TaskEditor with its typed text) is still in the navigator.
Widget test: on that route, type in the password field. The reason line stays visible.

Widget test: on that route, the `requestError` session sentence (`Vuelve a iniciar sesión para continuar. Tus tareas locales se conservan.`) isn't shown, and `Apunta lo que tienes que hacer y TaskFlow lo pone en tu calendario.` isn't shown.
Widget test: cold-start LoginScreen (no expired session) still shows `authPitch`, the email field is empty, and in create mode Back returns to sign-in.
Widget test: in Catalan at 2× text on 320×640, the sign-in-again route renders `S’ha tancat la sessió. Torna a entrar i continuaràs on ho havies deixat.` with no overflow.
ARB: `signInAgainReason` exists in app_en.arb, app_es.arb and app_ca.arb with the exact copy above.
deviceChecks: Expire the session from the server while typing a task: sign-in shows the reason line with the email filled in, Back leaves everything as it is, and signing in returns to the task with its text (with P30's open check).
